articles.title: Ben Simmons’ NBA comeback derailed after tearing achilles tendon in practice
articles.summary: Sacramento Kings guard to undergo surgery and will miss entire season. Former No 1 draft pick has been attempting to revive his career. Ben Simmons faces a monumental task to revive his NBA career after another devastating injury setback put his comeback attempt with the Sacramento Kings on hold.
body: The 30-year-old signed a one-year deal with the Kings in an attempt to revive his career, but will now miss the entire season. It is another massive setback for the three-time All-Star, after five years battling a series of significant injuries and mental health concerns.

“I’ve faced challenges before that tested me mentally, physically, and emotionally, and I’ve found a way through every single one of them,” Simmons posted in an Instagram story. “This injury is another chapter in my journey, not the end of my story.

“It’s never easy being away from the game I love, especially after everything it took to get back here. But if there’s one thing I’ve learned, it’s that adversity doesn’t define you. How you respond to it does. I’ve been knocked down before, and I’ve always found a way to get back up. This time will be no different.”

articles.title: Rays on verge of World Series return after Rasmussen dazzles in win over Guardians
articles.summary: Tampa Bay Rays 3-1 Cleveland Guardians. Rays lead best of seven series 3-2. Drew Rasmussen shines over seven innings. The Tampa Bay Rays moved to within one win of a return to the World Series on Sunday after defeating the Cleveland Guardians 3-1 to edge into a 3-2 lead in their MLB playoff series.
body: A dazzling pitching performance from starter Drew Rasmussen laid the foundation for another deserved victory for the Rays, who had leveled the best-of-seven American League Championship Series on Saturday.
Rasmussen restricted the Guardians to one run and four hits through seven innings with six strikeouts.
Rays catcher Liam Hicks paid tribute to Rasmussen’s gem after the win.

“He’s an ace, it’s as simple as that,” Hicks said. “He rises to the occasion and no moment is ever too big for him. I don’t think there’s anyone we’d rather have on the mound. He’s such a hard worker. He has a plan and then he just executes.”

articles.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
articles.summary: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different. At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively…
body: Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble.

How do you solve what is, on revenue versus results, the worst-run club in world football? By changing the name of the latest patsy on the touchline, of course. For now a hard-fought point is perhaps enough to stave off that pre-programmed emergency response.

Stand down the cowboy cops. Call off the blue and white saloons. Although with a run of Bournemouth, Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool next up in the league it will no doubt soon be time to go out there and arrest Lee Harvey Oswald again. What’s that you say? OK, well, dig him up again. Re-arrest him. Whatever it takes. Someone has to stop these lone gunmen, these managerial magic bullet merchants from derailing the Manchester United supremacy.

articles.title: Dana White Takes a Hilarious Dig at Sean Strickland After His Wild Canadian Adventure
articles.summary: Sean Strickland certainly made the most of his trip to Canada. The reigning middleweight champion travelled to the Great White North for UFC Edmonton, where he cornered Canadian fighter Melissa Croden in her preliminary bout against Chelsea Chandler.
body: But those were far from the wildest moments of Strickland’s visit. The outspoken American made a surprise appearance outside the Alberta Legislature, sporting a “Republic of Alberta” hoodie while delivering a speech in support of the province’s independence movement.

Strickland also found himself in hot water while livestreaming in downtown Edmonton. After filming people experiencing homelessness and open drug use, he was confronted by an angry woman who objected to being recorded. The encounter turned physical, with the woman slapping Strickland before chasing him down the street.
Naturally, Strickland’s eventful Canadian adventure became a talking point at the UFC Edmonton post-fight press conference, where Dana White had a hilarious response to the champion’s antics.

During the presser, a reporter asked White whether there were any issues between Strickland and the UFC following the fighter’s public complaints about his contract in recent weeks. White quickly dismissed the suggestion, saying, “There’s absolutely no issues with his contract. He just signed his contract in May.”

articles.title: 'Four points is nothing' - O'Neill stays cool after statement win
articles.summary: Amid supporter discontent, a recent protest against the major shareholder and a veteran manager deciding now is not the time to "wrap things up", as Martin O'Neill put it, you'd be forgiven for scratching your head when examining Celtic's current domestic situation.
body: They sit four points clear at the top of the Scottish Premiership. Five, really, if you factor in a goal difference at present 12 better than nearest challengers Rangers.

All this off the back of a 7-1 demolition of last season's runners-up, Hearts, who - at least until they turned up at Celtic Park - were widely viewed as viable title contenders if there's to be another three-way fight for Scottish football's main prize.
Has normal service been restored in the east end of Glasgow after the wobbles of four significant defeats in their past half-dozen? Not as far as their wily old manager is concerned.

Keen to stress that the road is yet long to the division's ultimate destination, O'Neill was full of smiles after his side's biggest win since he returned last year, but he didn't even accept that such a thrashing of the third-placed side in the division was even a 'statement' victory.

articles.title: Kirill Kaprizov breaks Wild record as hot start continues
articles.summary: Kirill Kaprizov breaks Wild record as hot start continues appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here. The Minnesota Wild are looking to return to the Stanley Cup Playoffs in 2027.
body: Kaprizov scored his 10th goal of the season in Sunday’s win over the Columbus Blue Jackets. His power-play goal in the second period gave Minnesota the goal they needed to claim a big 2-1 win. And it achieved a bit of history for the Wild star in the process.

The 29-year-old Kaprizov is now the fastest player in Wild franchise history to reach the 10-goal mark in a single season, according to NHL Public Relations. He needed just nine games to score 10 goals this year. Previously, the record was held by Brian Rolston, who needed 12 games to reach 10 goals in 2006-07.

The Wild star is also the first player in the league this season to score 10 goals. Entering play on Sunday, 18 players in the NHL had more than five goals, and five players had more than six, including Kaprizov. The next-best goal scorer in the league currently is Winnipeg Jets star Kyle Connor, who has eight goals.

Minnesota knows the sort of talent they have on their hands. They signed Kaprizov to a monster $136 million contract before the 2025-26 campaign. That contract kicked in back in July, and pays him $17 million a season until 2033-34.

articles.title: 5 Biggest Letdowns From NFL Week 6 on Sunday, Including A.J. Brown and the Rams
articles.summary: Another action-packed football Sunday is in the books, and now it’s time to reflect on the biggest letdowns from NFL Week 6. This week, that list includes A.J. Brown, but he’s certainly not alone.
body: It’s not that the Houston Texans are a bad team, but they came into Sunday’s matchup with just one win and four losses. Yet, as the Jacksonville Jaguars discovered, the Texans are still very capable. Still, London is supposed to be the Jaguars’ home away from home, but the Texans got the best of this four-win team on Sunday, pulling Houston a bit closer in the AFC South. The Jaguars lost by just three points, but allowed a season-high 114 rushing yards to a Texans team that’s had one of the NFL’s worst rushing offenses coming into the matchup.

When the New England Patriots traded a 2028 first-round pick for A.J. Brown, they envisioned Mike Vrabel’s former player to be an immediate fit in the offense. While he missed the past four weeks with a high ankle sprain, the Patriots are getting a horrible return on their investment. While Brown has a long time to make things right, after leaving his Patriots debut with the ankle injury following a lackluster 26-yard performance, he dropped a whopping four passes in Sunday’s game. That’s not acceptable for any receiver, let alone a three-time Pro Bowler.

articles.title: Arsenal win with one shot on target as Forest sink into bottom three
articles.summary: Arsenal's only shot on target proved enough to snatch victory at Nottingham Forest through Noni Madueke's deflected strike, keeping the champions within touching distance of Premier League leaders Manchester City and condemning Forest to the relegation zone.
body: After 80 frustrating minutes at the City Ground, substitute Madueke cut inside from the left and fired towards goal. His strike deflected off Jair Cunha, wrong-footed Matz Sels and found the net to settle a game in which Arsenal had struggled to turn possession into chances.

Arsenal had dominated the ball but registered no shots on target in the first half. Kai Havertz headed wide from a Declan Rice free-kick while Gabriel's set-piece effort was cleared almost off the line by Ousmane Diomande.

Forest made life difficult for Mikel Arteta's side, defending resolutely and threatening on the counter. Murillo almost salvaged a point in stoppage time with a superb solo run, driving at the Arsenal defence before curling narrowly wide. Ezri Konsa then made a crucial late challenge to deny Liam Delap.
However, despite their opportunities, it was the same old story for Oliver Glasner's side, who failed to find a breakthrough.
